rendered.overview: A five-color Commander deck built around [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], which draws a card whenever a permanent is airbent, earthbent, firebent or waterbent. It ramps with [[Shared Roots]] and [[Chromatic Lantern]], then fills the board with bending triggers from [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] while Lessons keep cards flowing. The backup win is [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] and the commander together making infinite creature tokens.

strategy: Cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3; each airbend, earthbend, firebend or waterbend draws a card.
Ramp with [[Shared Roots]] and [[Chromatic Lantern]], then airbend permanents with [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]].
Lessons like [[Airbending Lesson]] and [[Waterbending Lesson]] keep cards flowing while the board grows.
Backup: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] make infinite creature tokens.

keep: [[Shared Roots]] with [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] fuels an early airbend.
sendBack: Hands with no ramp and no [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] stall early.

tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] makes a 1/1 Ally token whenever you cast a spell from exile, such as one airbent by [[Aang, the Last Airbender]].

rendered.overview: Jeskai artifact deck built around [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], a hasty robot whose tap trigger proliferates counters each turn. Artifact mana sources and counter-adding creatures like [[Surge Conductor]] and [[Filigree Vector]] grow the board, and proliferate pieces such as [[Contagion Engine]] add more counters. It wins by growing attackers and artifact creatures until combat ends the game, with backup infinite lines in [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]].

strategy: Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3, then attack with it so each tap proliferates.
Ramp early with [[Everflowing Chalice]] and [[Pentad Prism]] to reach artifacts and the commander sooner.
Artifacts entering under [[Surge Conductor]] proliferate, and [[Filigree Vector]] adds counters on entry.
Backup win: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] together make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] early with a mana rock starts the proliferate engine.
sendBack: Only white lands with no blue or red source stalls the spells.
A hand lacking [[Surge Conductor]] and any ramp stalls the engine.

tips.text: [[Surge Conductor]] proliferates on each artifact entering, and [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] proliferates when tapped.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] makes every proliferate from [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] happen twice.
[[Throne of Geth]] and [[Filigree Vector]] each sacrifice an artifact to proliferate at will.

keyCards.job: Its tap trigger proliferates every counter in play.
Proliferates whenever another nontoken artifact enters.
Adds counters on entry, then proliferates by sacrifice.
Taps for three colorless, feeding the Zirda backup.
Cuts activation costs, enabling the Basalt backup loop.
Untaps its creature to enable the Unctus backup.
Its blue-creature trigger draws and discards for backups.

weaknesses: Moderate: [[Null Rod]] shuts off the many artifact mana sources and proliferate pieces at once.
Moderate: Six interaction cards, none mass removal, may not stop a fast combo; [[Swords to Plowshares]] answers only one creature.
Moderate: Losing [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] removes the main proliferate trigger, leaving [[Surge Conductor]] to carry the engine.

rendered.overview: This colorless Commander deck ramps with mana rocks and lands into big colorless spells, which cascade twice when cast from hand under [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]]. [[Ugin, the Ineffable]] and [[Eye of Ugin]] lower colorless costs so threats such as [[Kaldra Compleat]] arrive sooner. The commander is expected around turn 5. Its main win is stacked cascades and large colorless threats that overwhelm the table. As a backup, [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.

strategy: Ramp with [[Thran Dynamo]] and [[Basalt Monolith]], casting [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5.
Colorless spells of mana value 7 or more cast from hand cascade twice, as [[Kaldra Compleat]] does.
[[Ugin, the Ineffable]] and [[Eye of Ugin]] cut colorless costs so the big spells land sooner.
Backup win: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.

A cheap [[Ugin, the Ineffable]] discount helps big spells arrive sooner.
sendBack: Without ramp, a hand holding [[Kaldra Compleat]] stalls out.
Expensive spells with no [[Basalt Monolith]] or early mana stall.

[[Forsaken Monument]] adds an extra colorless to each permanent tapped for colorless, so [[Basalt Monolith]] makes more.

rendered.overview: A Naya Dinosaur deck built around [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]], which reveals cards and puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield whenever it deals combat damage. Nine ramp pieces aim to cast the commander around turn 7, then a wide board of Dinosaurs with haste and trample attacks to refill the battlefield each turn. [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] offer a mana-free backup route to infinite tokens.

strategy: Ramp with [[Farseek]], [[Topiary Stomper]] and [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] so its combat damage reveals and drops Dinosaurs; [[Regisaur Alpha]] adds a 3/3 token.
Each Dinosaur entering triggers [[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]] to discover, and [[Annoyed Altisaur]] cascades into a free spell.
Backup: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] together make infinite creature tokens for no mana.
Alternate win: [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Walking Ballista]] put infinite +1/+1 counters on most creatures you control.

keep: Early [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]] ramps into Dinosaurs on curve.
sendBack: Hands with no ramp and no early creature stall before the commander.
Hands missing Mountain or Plains sources cannot cast the Naya cards.

tips.text: [[Kinjalli's Caller]] and [[Knight of the Stampede]] each make Dinosaur spells cost less, and their reductions stack.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] pings every creature when a Dinosaur enters, so [[Polyraptor]] copies itself after that damage.
[[Wakening Sun's Avatar]] destroys non-Dinosaurs only when cast from hand, leaving [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and its Dinosaurs on board.

keyCards.job: Drops Dinosaurs from the top when it connects.
Discovers a card whenever a Dinosaur enters.
Gives other Dinosaurs haste and makes a 3/3.
Pings creatures each time a Dinosaur enters.
Copies itself whenever it is dealt damage.
Pings with its counters, pairing with [[Bellowing Aegisaur]].

weaknesses: Moderate: None of its 7 interaction cards is instant speed, so a fast combo like [[Thassa's Oracle]] can finish first.
Moderate: Without [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] the Dinosaurs lose their attack trigger, and [[Swords to Plowshares]] can remove it.
Moderate: Wins run through combat damage, so [[Propaganda]] taxing attacks stops Gishath and the Dinosaurs.

rendered.overview: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] taps to make a growing wave of Goblin tokens, and the mostly red Goblin deck swings with them while burn finishes the game. It runs 34 lands and six ramp pieces to reach its commander around turn 4. A backup route is [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Skirk Prospector]] beside [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], an infinite token combo.

strategy: Cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4, then tap it each turn for more Goblin tokens.
Add makers such as [[Dragon Fodder]] and [[Mogg War Marshal]], then attack with the Goblin wave.
Backup: [[Goblin Warchief]] with [[Skirk Prospector]] and [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] makes infinite Goblin tokens.
Finish stalled boards with burn such as [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Fireball]].

keep: Early [[Mogg War Marshal]] starts Goblins; ramp gets [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] out.
sendBack: Hands lacking any Goblin and any ramp stall before [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] lands.
A hand of only burn spells cannot start the Goblin token engine.

tips.text: [[Goblin Chieftain]] gives other Goblins +1/+1 and haste, so new [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] tokens attack the turn they appear.
[[Tar Pitcher]] sacrifices a Goblin to deal 2 damage, and [[Goblin Sledder]] sacrifices one for +1/+1.
[[Goblin Warchief]] makes Goblin spells cost one less, and [[Skirk Prospector]] turns a sacrificed Goblin into red mana.

keyCards.job: Taps for a growing wave of Goblin tokens.
Makes a Goblin on entering and on dying.
Makes Goblins haste and cuts Goblin spell costs.
Gives other Goblins haste and +1/+1.
Pings one target each time a Goblin dies.
Deals three damage to any target.

weaknesses: Moderate: Without [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] the token engine stops, and [[Swords to Plowshares]] answers it on sight.
Moderate: Fogs and pillowfort such as [[Propaganda]] stop the Goblin attacks the deck relies on.
Minor: No enchantment answer, so [[Journey to Nowhere]] can hold down [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for good.

rendered.overview: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] lead a Jeskai deck built around Gods: attacking with them banks experience counters, which feed counters onto a creature and fuel Atreus's card draw and 2 damage per activation. Nine ramp pieces aim to cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] around turn 4, and seven interaction cards clear blockers or answer threats. The deck wins by stacking counters over several attacks, drawing deep, and finishing opponents with direct damage.

strategy: Ramp with [[Talisman of Progress]] and [[Solemn Simulacrum]] toward casting [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] around turn 4.
Attack with Gods like [[God-Eternal Oketra]] and [[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] so [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] gains an experience counter each attack.
Kratos's end step puts counters on a creature; [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] then draws per counter for three mana.
Backup: [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] banks its own experience on attacks and makes Rebel tokens as an alternate swarm.

keep: [[God-Eternal Oketra]] with ramp in hand gives early God attacks.
Early ramp plus [[Solemn Simulacrum]] keeps the commander castable early.
sendBack: Hands missing blue or red sources can't cast the Jeskai spells.
Hands with no ramp and no God to attack with stall out.

tips.text: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] counters feed [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], whose ability draws one card per experience counter.
[[Surtr, Fiery Jötun]] deals 3 damage on each historic spell, and legendary [[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] counts as historic.

weaknesses: Moderate: Few answers to enchantments; [[Disenchant]] strips the non-creature Gods such as [[Thassa, God of the Sea]].
Moderate: Three of seven answers are instant speed, so a fast [[Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker]] combo can finish first.
Moderate: Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], no experience counters build, leaving [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s draw and damage idle.

backups: Backup: [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] banks its own experience counter on each attack and makes Rebel tokens for an alternate swarm.

rendered.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a Dimir ninja deck that wins by connecting with unblocked attackers and swapping them for Ninjas through ninjutsu. Each Ninja that hits reveals the top card into hand and drains each opponent by that card's mana value. [[Satoru Umezawa]] looks at three cards on every ninjutsu, and [[Changeling Outcast]], [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] and [[Tormented Soul]] supply the unblockable attackers. Extra turns from [[Time Warp]] are a second route to victory.

strategy: Attack with [[Changeling Outcast]] or another unblockable creature, then ninjutsu a Ninja in once it goes unblocked.
Each Ninja that deals combat damage makes [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] reveal the top card into hand and drain.
[[Satoru Umezawa]] looks at three cards on every ninjutsu, so each hit adds more cards to hand.
Backup: [[Time Warp]] and [[Temporal Mastery]] give extra turns to attack again once the board is set.

keep: [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] plus a cheap attacker starts it.
[[Mistblade Shinobi]] and a cheap attacker make an early swap.
sendBack: No blue or black source means no ninjutsu early.
No creature to attack with means nothing to swap for a Ninja.

tips.text: [[Satoru Umezawa]] looks at the top three on each ninjutsu, while [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] reveals a card when a Ninja hits.
[[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] can enter by commander ninjutsu, returning an unblocked [[Mistblade Shinobi]] to hand so it can be cast again.
[[Dokuchi Silencer]] can discard a creature card on hit to destroy a creature, while [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] draws a card on hit.
